mentions.name: ProxyML
mentions.description: ProxyML explains ML predictions without direct access to the underlying data or model. Users provide basic statistics about their data, which are used to generate synthetic data; a surrogate model is then trained to predict the target model's predictions on that synthetic data. Aimed at model risk management and governance, such as creating challenger models for SR 11-7 compliance without the hassle of obtaining the original data or setting up the black-box model. It is available as a Python SDK, a schema builder, and a hosted service.
mentions.problem: Model risk management and governance (e.g., SR 11-7 challenger models) normally requires gaining access to the original data and setting up the black-box model; the author previously had to build throwaway models just to justify needing a better one.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I had an idea about explaining ML predictions without direct access to the data or the model:  provide basic stats about your data, use them to generate synthetic data, then train a surrogate to predict your model's predictions on the synthetic data.

Could be handy for model risk management and governance, e.g. if you need a challenger model for SR 11-7 without all the hassle of getting access to the original data, getting the black box model set up, and so on.
